description:
Found by s507d (the pcl documentation batch) while checking the claim "-c runs BEGIN blocks and use as perl -c does".  Probed against perl 5.40.3 on main 50dbd195 (= 08de9e4f + records).

Reproducer 1 (the mechanism):
  perl -e 'CHECK { print "chk\n" } use List::Util; BEGIN { print "b\n" }'   -> b / chk
  pcl  -e 'CHECK { print "chk\n" } use List::Util; BEGIN { print "b\n" }'   -> chk / b
  Same with `use POSIX ();` and `use File::Basename;`.  With no `use`, or only pragmas (`use strict;`), the order is right.

Reproducer 2 (what a user sees, `pcl -c`):
  printf 'use strict;\nuse warnings;\nuse File::Basename;\nuse NoSuchModuleXyz;\nprint 1;\n' > c9.pl
  perl -c c9.pl  -> Can't locate NoSuchModuleXyz.pm ... BEGIN failed--compilation aborted at c9.pl line 4.  exit 2
  pcl  -c c9.pl  -> c9.pl syntax OK  exit 0
  printf 'use List::Util qw(sum);\nBEGIN { die "begin died\n" }\nprint sum(1,2), "\n";\n' > c7.pl
  perl -c c7.pl  -> begin died / BEGIN failed  exit 2;   pcl -c c7.pl -> syntax OK, exit 0
  printf 'use List::Util qw(sum);\nBEGIN { print STDOUT "b\n" }\nprint 3, "\n";\n' > c2.pl
  perl -c c2.pl  -> b on stdout;  pcl -c c2.pl -> nothing on stdout

`pcl -c` is PCLSwitches::expand_program's `CHECK { print STDERR "NAME syntax OK\n"; close STDOUT; require POSIX; POSIX::_exit(0) }` put in front of the program; that is right only if CHECK runs after the whole compile phase.  The phase model across sections (the first non-pragma `use` starts a new section?) runs the CHECK at the end of the FIRST section.  Fix belongs to the phase model, not to -c.  docs/pcl-commands.md's "where pcl differs from perl" table names this until it is fixed.


=== DONE (s507c, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) ===
MEASUREMENT TAKEN FIRST: the emission of a MODULE ends its compile phase with the same `(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)` as a program (pl2cl --module lib/List/Util.pm: line 749), and that function drained the GLOBAL *check-blocks* / *init-blocks* and set *p-compile-phase-done*.  So the first module a program `use`d ran the PROGRAM's queued CHECK and INIT blocks at the module's boundary.  On the text path (-e, -c, any source switch, --no-cache) that is the chk/b inversion; on the script-cache fasl path the compile-time `use` had already loaded the module before the CHECK was pushed, which is why a plain `pcl file.pl` looked right.  The first `pcl -e` run printed only "b": the module's fasl build muffles STDOUT and the drained CHECK printed into it (#2702's family).
FIX (the phase model, not -c): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-load-unit` wraps p-load-module-cached and p-load-extension: fresh UNITCHECK/CHECK/INIT queues and *p-unit-load* t; under *p-unit-load* p-run-compile-phase-blocks runs the unit's UNITCHECK only; on a normal return the unit's CHECK/INIT are spliced on top of the caller's queues (newest first, like a push) while the main program compiles, and dropped once it runs (perl's "too late").  ir-spec §9.0a (normative + one example).  This also CLOSES #1201 (a used module's CHECK now runs; a run-time require's does not).
PROBE TABLE (scratch/s507c/m1/, perl -> base ac2fec1e -> tree, text path and cached path): p01 CHECK/use/BEGIN; p02 BEGIN/CHECK/INIT/END x2 around a module with CHECK/INIT/UNITCHECK/BEGIN/body; p03 run-time require (CHECK/INIT must NOT run); p04 three sections + two module uses; p05 two package blocks; p06/p07 CHECK in eval STRING (does not run; the "Too late" WARNING is warnings-gated, absent -- #221 class); p08 main UNITCHECK vs module's; p09 exit in CHECK; c9/c7/c2 = the task's three -c reproducers.  Every row = perl on the tree except: p07 (the warning), c7's exit status (255 vs 2: $! after the @INC search, PRE-EXISTING, filed #2740) and the "While evaluating the form" prefix (#2492, s507b).  The base failed p02/p03/p04(text)/p05(text)/p08/c9/c7/c2.  The module CHECK's position on a script's CACHE-BUILDING run is still #2702's (the module loads at the build's compile time).
GUARD: Pl/t/phase-units-01.t, 9 rows (all 9 FAIL on the base extraction).  docs/pcl-commands.md: the -c differs-table row loses its "known bug" sentence.
BARS (7bc12f4c = main eae5812c + the batch): gate PASS 279 files / 9,758 rows; sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18731 (+0), the 5 UNSTABLE rows identical on the base; gate-set-scan both populations (638 files) IDENTICAL; companion --all --quick: comp/hints.t 16/13 -> 17/12 (row 9, the CHECK-time row) spliced; EVERYDAY 113 -> 113.
subject: SILENT WRONG under `pcl -c` (found by s507d, on main 50dbd195): a CHECK block that precedes a `use` of a non-pragma module runs BEFORE the later BEGIN blocks and `use` lines -- `pcl -e 'CHECK { print "chk\n" } use List::Util; BEGIN { print "b\n" }'` prints chk/b, perl b/chk -- so `pcl -c` (whose expansion IS a first CHECK block) says "syntax OK", exit 0, for `use strict; use warnings; use File::Basename; use NoSuchModuleXyz;` where perl dies "Can't locate", exit 2
